[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The EventBridge target can begin delivering scheduled events as soon as it is created, but the Lambda invoke permission is provisioned independently. Make the target wait for its invoke permission to avoid a window where scheduled invocations are denied.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The EventBridge target can be installed and the schedule can fire before Lambda's invoke permission is granted. Add an explicit ordering dependency so the target is not active before its permission exists.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The EventBridge target can be registered before the Lambda invoke permission exists. The rule may then attempt delivery while invocation is still denied; make the target wait for the permission.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The scheduled scale-down target can become active before EventBridge has permission to invoke the Lambda. Order target creation after its Lambda permission to avoid a period of failed scheduled invocations.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The scheduled scale-down target can become active before its Lambda invoke permission is granted; order target creation after the permission.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The scheduled EventBridge target can become active before its Lambda invoke permission is installed. Ensure the target is not registered until this permission exists.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
This scheduled pool target can be activated before its EventBridge invoke permission exists. The target should wait for the corresponding Lambda permission so scheduled invocations are authorized from the outset.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The scheduled pool target can be installed before the corresponding Lambda invoke permission exists, allowing a scheduled invocation to fail during deployment. Make the target depend on the permission.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The EventBridge target may be registered and start invoking the pool Lambda before its Lambda invoke permission is installed. Order target creation after the permission.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
Creating this trigger object immediately generates an S3 event for the syncer Lambda. The syncer execution role's S3 policy is provisioned independently, so the first invocation could run before its required bucket access is granted.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The deployment trigger uploads an S3 object that invokes the syncer, but it is not ordered after the syncer's S3 access policy is attached. The first invocation can run before the Lambda role has the permissions needed to read/write the distribution bucket; add an ordering dependency before uploading the trigger object.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The deployment trigger object is deliberately written after the bucket notification is configured, which can immediately invoke the syncer Lambda. It does not wait for the syncer's S3 access policy, so the first invocation can run before the execution role is authorized to access the distribution object. Order the trigger object after this policy.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The event source mapping can begin polling and invoking the scale-up Lambda when created. It should wait until the Lambda execution role policy granting the required queue and scale-up permissions has been applied.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The SQS event source mapping can begin polling before the Lambda execution role's SQS permissions are attached, leaving the mapping unable to consume messages during deployment. Make the mapping depend on the scale-up role policy.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The SQS event source mapping can be enabled before the scale-up Lambda execution role has the inline policy granting access to the build queue. Ensure the mapping waits for this policy so polling/invocation does not begin with insufficient role permissions.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The GitHub App webhook is configured using the API endpoint, but the app update can run before the API Gateway route is deployed. Waiting for the route (which depends on the integration) avoids registering an endpoint that is not yet functional.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The GitHub App webhook URL is updated from the API's endpoint and a local path, but that value does not wait for the API Gateway route to be created. The app can start sending webhook requests before the route is configured; make the update wait for the route.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The GitHub App update can run before the default API Gateway stage exists, even though its endpoint requires that stage to be callable. Order the app update after stage creation.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The GitHub App update can run before API Gateway's default stage is ready and auto-deployed, so the configured endpoint may not yet serve the route. Make the update wait for the stage.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
module.webhook-github-app:resource.null_resource.update_app registers the GitHub App webhook via local-exec using the endpoint URL built from module.multi-runner:output.webhook. That endpoint value only references aws_apigatewayv2_api.webhook.api_endpoint, not the $default stage, so Terraform can run the local-exec (and GitHub will start delivering webhooks to the URL) before module.multi-runner.module.webhook:resource.aws_apigatewayv2_stage.webhook exists / has auto-deployed the POST /webhook route — the endpoint would then return errors until the stage deploys. The null_resource should be ordered after the stage is created.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
The GitHub App webhook registration in null_resource.update_app should also wait for the API Gateway stage to be deployed ($default with auto_deploy). The stage has no dependency on the route in the current graph and the null_resource has no dependency on the stage at all, so the local-exec can run against an API endpoint that is not yet serving traffic. An explicit depends_on is needed since the endpoint output references only the API resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The null_resource 'update_app' reconfigures the GitHub App to deliver webhooks to the API Gateway endpoint (module.multi-runner.webhook.endpoint). Its only ordering comes from the webhook output, which resolves to the aws_apigatewayv2_api object (plus the webhook lambda, log group, and role). It has no dependency on the aws_apigatewayv2_stage ('$default', auto_deploy) — nor on the aws_apigatewayv2_route/integration behind it — so Terraform may run the update-app.sh local-exec while the stage that makes the endpoint serve traffic is still being created, briefly pointing the GitHub App webhook at a non-functional URL. Add a depends_on for the webhook stage so the endpoint is deployed before the GitHub App is updated.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The GitHub App can be configured to send webhook calls before API Gateway has permission to invoke the Lambda. Make the app update wait for the API Gateway Lambda permission.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The GitHub App can be updated with the API endpoint before API Gateway has permission to invoke its Lambda. This can cause initial webhook deliveries to fail; make the update wait for the Lambda permission as well as the route and stage.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The scheduled syncer target may invoke Lambda as soon as the target is installed. The function's execution role needs this S3 policy to access the distribution bucket, but target creation is not ordered after that policy; wait for it to avoid early invocations failing authorization.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The EventBridge schedule can invoke the syncer as soon as its target is registered, but the syncer's S3 access policy is created independently. Ensure the scheduled target is not enabled until the execution role has the S3 permissions needed by the function.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The API Gateway route can become active while its Lambda invoke permission is still being created, so early webhook requests may fail. Ensure the route is created only after the permission is in place.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The API Gateway route uses an integration, but the Lambda permission is separately created and does not order the API integration or route. Ensure the permission exists before the route is created, so the API cannot be exposed before Lambda allows invocation.
